summary: Build practical AI safety controls, risk registers and governance dashboards. Enrol in this applied AI governance course.
lede: Operational AI safety, governance and compliance helps organizations turn responsible AI principles into practical oversight across the AI lifecycle. Using ISO/IEC 42001 as a management-system reference, supported by the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, ISO/IEC 23894 and ISO/IEC 27001:2022, the course covers AI inventory management, risk classification, model lifecycle governance, control assurance and incident reporting. You will build an AI risk register, map controls, assess impacts, document human oversight and prepare evidence for boards, auditors, customers and funding partners. Practical exercises include model cards, third-party assessment checklists, governance metrics, action plans and reporting packs designed to support proportionate control in complex operating environments.
audienceIntro: This AI governance course is designed for professionals who approve, operate, assure or report on AI and automation across regulated and public-interest environments. It suits mixed-experience teams because technical concepts receive practical explanation while governance outputs receive applied workshop time.
modules: AI Governance Foundations and Risk Context
AI Inventory, Impact and Risk Assessment
AI Security and Technical Control Integration
AI Governance Roadmap and Executive Integration
prerequisites: You should have working exposure to risk management, compliance, cybersecurity, data governance, technology operations or AI-enabled business processes. No coding or programming is required. You should bring one representative AI or automation use case, if available, with sensitive information removed. Advanced AI engineering, machine-learning development and statistical model validation are introduced at conceptual awareness level rather than taught as implementation skills.
